title: Nigeria History Tracker Update — May 21, 2026
summary: A landmark US-Nigeria joint AFRICOM operation killed ISIS global #2 Abu-Bilal al-Minuki and approximately 175 ISWAP fighters across three rounds of strikes (May 16–18), representing the most effective single-week attrition against the northeast insurgency in years. Simultaneously, Nigeria suffered its worst wave of school abductions since 2021: Boko Haram seized 42–82 students in Borno's Askira-Uba LGA while bandits abducted 46 in Oyo's Oriire LGA — one teacher was later beheaded, triggering national outrage and Senate condemnation. The EFCC arrested fugitive ex-Power Minister Saleh Mamman after his in-absentia 75-year fraud conviction. The CBN held its MPR at 26.5% even as April inflation ticked up to 15.69%, drawing sharp economist criticism. New map points added for Kukawa, Wulgo MNJTF base, Askira-Uba, Oriire LGA, and the Metele strike zone.

title: Nigeria History Tracker Update — May 09, 2026
summary: ISWAP launched coordinated back-to-back assaults on FOB Magumeri in Borno (May 7) and the 27 Brigade HQ in Yobe (May 9), killing four soldiers total and marking the most intense ISWAP offensive against fixed army installations in 2026. On the political front, Nigeria's opposition parties agreed to field a single presidential candidate for 2027, while the xenophobic killings of Nigerians in South Africa triggered a diplomatic standoff and House of Representatives resolution calling for sanctions. Economically, the naira stabilized near ₦1,374/$ with the IMF raising Nigeria's 2026 growth forecast to 4.1%, while the NLC led nationwide May Day protests demanding a minimum wage rise to ₦154,000 amid inflation of 15.38%. New map points added for the Plateau State conflict zone, FOB Magumeri, and the Yobe 27 Brigade area.
